{"additions":523,"author":{"is_bot":true,"login":"app/entire"},"baseRefName":"main","body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/831
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

**What:** SessionStart no longer dials the network synchronously to refresh the trails-enablement cache.

**Why / how it helps:** Users reported Claude Code startup/exit getting noticeably slower with Entire hooks enabled, and that the latency disappeared when hooks were removed. Profiling traced it to `handleLifecycleSessionStart`'s trails-enablement cache refresh, which called `TrailsEnabled` on the API synchronously whenever the hourly cache was unknown or stale (first session in a repo, TTL expiry, or a changed auth key). Against a slow or unreachable host (VPN, firewall, flaky network) this blocked the hook for up to `trailEnablementSessionStartRefreshTimeout` (1s) on every affected session start, since the underlying `/.well-known/entire-api.json` discovery dial has no fast local/offline path.

**How:** The refresh now runs in a detached subprocess (`entire __refresh_trail_enablement`), spawned only when a local, network-free cache check finds the value unknown — mirroring the existing detached-analytics pattern in `cmd/entire/cli/telemetry`. The detached child runs from the worktree root (`cmd.Dir`) and inherits the parent's environment, so it resolves the same git-common-dir clone-preferences file and the same enablement scope (repo key, API base, auth key) the parent reads back — the cache the parent reads is the cache the child writes. The "forge not supported" case is still answered locally with no spawn. SessionStart itself only resolves the enablement scope (local git remote + auth-key lookup, no network) and decides whether to spawn; it never blocks on `TrailsEnabled`. Stop and SessionEnd (the exit-side hooks) were already fast — the refresh only ever ran on SessionStart — so this scopes the fix to the one hot path.

**Testing:**
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint` — 0 issues; `go build ./...` clean including a `GOOS=windows` cross-build (all three platform spawn files compile)
- `mise run test:ci` / full `cmd/entire/cli` package suite green (2489 tests). A pre-existing `TestExternalCommand_SigintReachesPlugin` flake under full-suite load reproduces identically on unmodified `main` and passes in isolation on both `main` and this branch (unrelated to this change)
- Added `TestHandleLifecycleSessionStart_NoSynchronousNetworkForTrailEnablement`: SessionStart hands the refresh to the detached-spawn seam exactly once and returns in well under 1s. The API base points at a blackholed https host that accepts the TCP connection but never answers; because `api.RequireSecureURL` rejects plain http before any dial, the host must be https for a synchronous regression to actually reach it — a regression to inline dialing then trips all three assertions (spawn hand-off, `dialed > 0`, ~1s block). Mutation-verified by reverting the fix to a synchronous refresh (all three assertions fired; observed `dialed=1`, `elapsed≈1.03s`)
- Added `TestRunTrailEnablementRefresh_BoundedByTimeoutAgainstUnresponsiveHost`: the deferred refresh itself still gives up within its own timeout against a host that accepts connections but never responds (no hang). Mutation-verified by removing the internal timeout (the call ran ~8s and the test failed)
- Excluded the hidden `__refresh_trail_enablement` command from the post-run checkpoint-policy warning, matching its sibling `__send_analytics`, so the detached child skips a pointless repo-open + local policy read (`TestShouldCheckCheckpointPolicyWarning` extended)
- Diagnosability: the detached child now initializes file logging and `runTrailEnablementRefresh` logs its scope/auth/network outcome at debug, so a failing background refresh (the #450 unreachable-host symptom) is visible in `.entire/logs/entire.log` instead of vanishing to discarded stderr (`TestRefreshTrailEnablementCmd_LogsBackgroundFailureToFile`, mutation-verified by removing the log init and the log call)
- Spawn throttle: a flock-guarded per-repo marker keyed to the shared git-common-dir collapses a burst of SessionStart hooks to ~one detached refresh child per refresh-timeout window — without it an unreachable host (which never writes the cache, so the TTL never starts) forked a fresh repo-open + auth + dial child on every session start (`TestTrailRefreshRecentlySpawned_ThrottlesWithinWindow` + `TestSpawnDetachedTrailEnablementRefresh_CollapsesBurst`, mutation-verified)
- Live measurement (10-run medians, `entire hooks claude-code session-start` invoked directly with a representative payload, network isolated via env-only `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME`):
  - stale cache + blackholed API host — before: ~1030ms every call; after: ~35-40ms
  - warm cache / fast-failing network — before and after: ~35-40ms (unchanged)
  - `stop` / `session-end` hooks — ~40-50ms before and after (unaffected; refresh only ran on SessionStart)

Fixes #450

319	// through to spawning — never worse than before this guard existed.
320	func trailRefreshRecentlySpawned(commonDir string, now time.Time) bool {
321		dir := filepath.Join(commonDir, "entire")
322		// Create the directory before acquiring the lock: flock.Acquire opens the
323		// lock file, which fails if its parent doesn't exist yet (mirrors
324		// ModifyClonePreferences, which MkdirAlls before locking).
325		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o750); err != nil {
326			return false
327		}
328		markerPath := filepath.Join(dir, "trail-refresh-spawn")
329		release, err := flock.Acquire(markerPath + ".lock")
330		if err != nil {
331			return false
332		}
333		defer release()
334	
335		if data, readErr := os.ReadFile(markerPath); readErr == nil { //nolint:gosec // markerPath is derived from the trusted git-common-dir, not user input
336			if last, parseErr := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, strings.TrimSpace(string(data))); parseErr == nil &&
337				now.After(last) && now.Sub(last) < trailRefreshSpawnThrottle {
338				return true
339			}
340		}
341		//nolint:errcheck // best-effort marker; a failed write just means the next hook re-spawns
342		_ = os.WriteFile(markerPath, []byte(now.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)), 0o600)
343		return false
344	}
